_comment: The hand-written half. Edit this daily; fetch-data.mjs merges it with FRED and never overwrites it.
summary: Oil is down 16% on the month and the 10 year is at a one month high. Read that twice. Brent is $91 and crude is $85, with the IEA pointing to better Middle East supply and plenty of physical barrels. The thing that caused this inflation is going away, and yields went up anyway. What does this even mean? Core inflation rose more than expected in October, and that is the whole story. The oil shock already seeped into core services, so it stopped being an oil problem and became a wage and services problem. Cheaper crude does not fix that. The market has now fully priced a 25bp hike in December and more next year. The 2 year is *4.84%* and the real 10 year, the one after inflation, is 2.91%. That is the highest cost of real money since 2008. Also, something new. Treasuries did not catch a bid during the AI selloff this time. Funds are liquidating bonds to raise cash as AI infrastructure stocks unwind. Recall: for two months the answer was always flight to safety. Not anymore. When the selling gets big enough, people sell what they can, not what they want. Mixing this all in a pot: cheap oil, hot core, a hiking Fed, and a forced seller in the bond market. December is no longer a question.
_fedPath_note: Every FOMC decision since the last hike, oldest first: the date, the upper bound of the target range after it, and hike / cut / hold. Drawn as the staircase under the Fed and listed in its card. Add a row after each meeting.

news.what: Market now fully prices a 25bp hike in December, and more next year. Core inflation rising faster than expected says the oil shock has seeped into core services.
Treasuries did not catch a bid during the AI selloff. Funds are liquidating bonds to raise cash as AI infrastructure stocks unwind.
Brent below $94 and crude below $86. The IEA points to improving Middle East supply and ample physical availability.
Continuing jobless claims tested their lowest level in over three years.
October CPI: headline +0.4% MoM and core +0.3%, both above expectations. No year over year rate published, last year's shutdown left no base month.
Payrolls +165,000 in October against 65,000 expected. August and September revised up by a combined 84,000.
Fed held at 3.75-4.00%. Two policymakers voted to hike.

_curve_note: Optional hand entry for a yield FRED has not published yet. Same rule as oil: only used while newer than FRED. notes/alert are display only. Put alert on whatever the day's story is: it turns the figure rust and is the only thing telling a first-time visitor where to look. strain is the quieter version: a smaller crack on the summit, number stays in ink. track is [open, low, now] for one tenor's day, drawn as a path under the summit; use it only when the path matters more than the close, and leave it out otherwise.
